title: Superposition and Wave Function Collapse
text:
In quantum physics, superposition describes a state where a particle exists simultaneously in all possible measurable states. This means that before an observation is made, the particle's properties (such as position or momentum) are not fixed to a single value but rather represent a weighted combination of possibilities.

The act of measurement fundamentally alters this system. The process of observation forces the quantum state to 'collapse' from its superposition into one definite eigenvalue. This collapse transforms probabilistic existence into measurable certainty, adhering to core tenets of quantum theory.

This mechanism distinguishes quantum systems from classical physics, suggesting that objective reality at the subatomic level is inherently indeterminate until an interaction—specifically, measurement—takes place.
